expected_evidence: geological: anomalous sediment layer ('black mat') at ~12,900 cal BP across North American sites, containing platinum/iridium spikes, nanodiamonds, magnetic spherules, glassy carbon spherules, and elevated soot/charcoal indicating widespread biomass burning
astronomical: physical impactor debris (extraterrestrial chondritic material, shocked quartz, high-temperature melt-glass) or a confirmed impact crater/airburst structure dated to the YD onset
material (archaeological): abrupt disruption or abandonment horizon at Clovis-era sites, correlated megafauna extinction layer, and reduced/altered lithic assemblages immediately above the black mat
genetic: population bottleneck signatures in North American megafauna and/or early human (Paleoindian) mtDNA lineages dated to ~10,950 BCE

model_prior (unverified, from training data, not from the evidence text): ongoing scientific literature debate (Firestone et al. 2007 proposing the impact; multiple subsequent papers failing to replicate nanodiamond/platinum signals or proposing alternative causes like meltwater-pulse/AMOC shutdown) - reflects general recollection of the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis controversy, not confirmed fact
oral_tradition: flood/catastrophe narratives sometimes speculatively linked to the event, though such linkage is highly uncertain and largely unverifiable this far back
iconographic: none expected — no symbolic/artistic record-keeping tradition existed in North America at this time depth
response.rationale: This hypothesis corresponds to the real-world Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (YDIH), and the action field correctly marks it 'inconclusive' — matching genuine scientific controversy status (model-prior, unverified against the evidence text provided here). The strongest expected evidence channel is geological (detectability 0.65 for the younger-dryas period): sedimentary 'black mat' layers, platinum anomalies, and spherules have been reported at numerous North American sites in the literature I recall, so absence-of-evidence arguments carry less weight here — some geological evidence plausibly did survive and was found, consistent with an 'inconclusive' rather than a fully 'refuted' or fully 'confirmed' status. Astronomical evidence (a confirmed crater or unambiguous extraterrestrial material) has a nominally high detectability score (0.7) but is intrinsically hard to obtain for an airburst (which by definition may leave no crater) or for an impact into ice/ocean that would erode or be lost over ~13,000 years — this explains the practical absence of a smoking-gun impactor despite the high nominal detectability score. Material/archaeological (0.35) and genetic (0.3) evidence are moderately detectable but coarse-grained, well suited to correlating extinction/disruption timing but not to establishing causation. Textual (0.0) and iconographic (0.1) evidence are essentially inapplicable given no writing systems existed in North America at this time depth. I adjust the composite detectability slightly downward from the raw geological figure (0.65) toward a blended estimate of 0.55, reflecting that while geological signals are moderately detectable and partially reported, the decisive astronomical/impactor evidence needed to move this from 'inconclusive' to 'confirmed' is disproportionately hard to detect (airburst mechanisms leave weak physical traces), which is the main reason the hypothesis remains unresolved rather than because it is false.
